I will keep the land in the wheat-maize rotation I know best. In Quzhou County, that is the safest way for me to use the whole year, spread labor, and protect my income. I am 76, so I will not choose crops that need fine management or too much hand work. I will finish the winter wheat that is already in the field, then plant summer maize right after harvest so the land does not sit idle. I will use improved seed rather than anything fancy, put most fertilizer on the maize and a moderate amount on the wheat, irrigate only as many times as I think the crop truly needs, and keep tillage simple with rotary work because it is easier and faster for me to manage. I will spray only when I think pests or disease are likely to cut yield. I am aiming for steady production, not taking risks for the highest possible yield.
